name: Open an authentic looking R760 cutaway
description: The initial live cutaway presents a full 2U rack server instead of a generic drive-like box.
steps: Identify the PowerEdge R760 title and 3D model
Inspect the 3D model and locate front drive carriers, cooling fans, CPU heatsinks and rear risers
expected: A large interactive rack server is shown. The server has 16 front drive carriers, a row of six cooling fans, metallic dual CPU heatsinks, green motherboard and memory, rear expansion risers, and a metal chassis.

name: Inspect actual component groups
description: Click component index items to understand real server hardware.
steps: In Explore mode click DDR5 memory in the component index
Use the Dell service manual link
expected: The detail panel updates to describe 32 DIMM positions, then two Xeon PHMs, and the Dell service manual link works.

name: Follow the guided access path
description: The step-by-step path walks through cover removal, air shroud, risers, fan cage, and CPU access.
steps: Press Next to remove the system cover
Press Next to lift the air shroud
Advance through several subsequent steps using Next and Previous
expected: The numbered progress advances through 13 distinct steps; each step gives a real component, grounded description, and relevant safety note; the 3D model changes.

name: Disassemble and reassemble using slider
description: A phone user can separate the server and return it to the open cutaway.
steps: On mobile switch to Explore mode
Move Separate server components slider to 100%
expected: The 3D components separate and reassemble, the percentage text updates, the slider remains usable and the mobile controls do not overflow.

name: Navigate component selection on mobile
description: All hardware systems remain reachable and their information readable on small screens.
steps: On mobile scroll the component row horizontally
expected: Component headings, descriptions and hardware details update correctly. The viewport and content remain readable.
